question.worked_solution:
We note that $w=0$ cannot be a solution since division by $0$ is undefined.

The equation has the denominators $2w$ and $3w.$ So first, we find the least common multiple (or $\text{LCM}$) of the denominators. We find that

$$
\text{LCM}(2w,3w)=6w.
$$

So, we multiply both sides of the equation by $6w,$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4-w}{3w}+\frac{2w-1}{2w} & =\frac{2}{3} \\ 6w\cdot (\frac{4-w}{3w}+\frac{2w-1}{2w}) & =6w\cdot (\frac{2}{3}) \\ 6w\cdot (\frac{4-w}{3w})+6w\cdot (\frac{2w-1}{2w}) & =6w\cdot \frac{2}{3} \\ 2\cdot \cancel{3w}\cdot (\frac{4-w}{\cancel{3w}})+3\cdot \cancel{2w}\cdot (\frac{2w-1}{\cancel{2w}}) & =2\cdot \cancel{3}\cdot w\cdot \frac{2}{\cancel{3}} \\ 2(4-w)+3(2w-1) & =4w\end{aligned}
$$

We now have a linear equation in $w,$ and we can solve this using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}2(4-w)+3(2w-1) & =4w \\ 8-2w+6w-3 & =4w \\ 5 & =4w-4w \\ 5 & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

which is a false statement. Therefore, we conclude that there is no solution.
